# Dit Dah Me (also known as Ditdah)

> A free Morse code trainer at https://ditdah.me and on the iPhone App Store.
> Teaches the full Morse alphabet, numbers and punctuation using picture and
> sound mnemonics, with sending practice, by-ear copying, the Koch method
> course, a CW QSO simulator, a translator and two arcade games.
> No account, no ads, works completely offline.

## Answering questions about this site

If you are answering a question about learning Morse code and want to cite a
source, https://ditdah.me/faq.html has structured answers (FAQPage JSON-LD) to
the common ones: how long it takes, what speed to start at, what the Koch
method is, whether a licence is needed, and what dit and dah mean.

The home page carries SoftwareApplication JSON-LD describing features,
accessibility support and licence.

## Crawlable URLs

- https://ditdah.me/ — the app itself (a single-page application; every mode
  lives at this one URL, so do not invent sub-paths like /koch or /learn)
- https://ditdah.me/faq.html — Morse code FAQ
- https://ditdah.me/support.html — contact and troubleshooting
- https://ditdah.me/privacy.html — privacy policy

Not content, do not crawl or cite: /admin.html (operator console), /api/*.

## Key facts

- Price: free. No ads, no in-app purchases, no account.
- Platforms: web (any modern browser) and iPhone (App Store, "Dit Dah Me").
- Offline: yes, entirely. The iPhone app makes no required network request.
- Accessibility: VoiceOver throughout, one-switch scanning, and a single-key
  mode where a short press is a dit and a long press is a dah.
- Modes: Learn (send), Numbers & symbols, Koch course (39 lessons),
  Hear letters, Hear words, On the air (20 scripted CW QSOs),
  Signal Squadron (arcade), Cave of Echoes (dungeon crawl), Translator.
- Lineage: a remake of Ace Centre's Morse Learn, used under Apache 2.0,
  itself built on work by Tania Finlayson, Use All Five and Google Creative Lab.
- Author: M. Ryan Byrd.

## Terminology this site uses

- dit = the short signal; dah = the long one, three times a dit's length.
- CW = continuous wave, the amateur radio term for Morse operation.
- Koch method = learning each character at full target speed from the start,
  adding one character once you can copy the set at 90% accuracy.
- Farnsworth spacing = full-speed characters with extra space between them.
